independentReview.findingSummary: Both independently identified P2 issues are closed at the reviewed final-v2 bytes and bounded evidence. No other definite P1/P2 was established; conditional runtime risks are retained below.
productionAssessment: Pure persistLoginInfo is a distinct traditional operation with bounded string Map and timeout. Its branch does not call getLoginJs, evaluate a prelude/login/action, infer a header or accept UI events. Empty Map removes only login-info; rejected put is a non-ACK DTO and rejected removal/IO/cancel remains error.

It uses the existing same-source gate/executor/process and checked source.login-info credential owner. After waiting for the gate, the current source resolver checks UUID/URL/full definition signature. All old grant, host deadline, source ownership and keychain revision notification paths remain the actual owners.

MayCommit and Committed are retained independently on host error/cancellation, session close failure and post-receipt cancellation. The App copies receipt effects before its cancellation check and logs only codes/counts. No UI transient map is written merely because a callback is transported.

The existing View keeps working Map separate from text controls. Semantic missing/empty select/toggle construction carries workingMapChanged; callbacks/select/toggle/dynamic re-render mark dirty while text edits alone do not. Valid OK marks sticky oKToClose before async work and does not reset on failure/cancel.

Actual Close snapshots only working Map, invalidates/cancels prior actions/form/render, awaits each owned task before checked persistence, and permits dismissal only on exact ACK or explicit abandonment. Repeated disappearance shares one exit task; own log/browser child covers do not trigger form exit. Forced parent disappearance keeps the frozen owned task with existing BackgroundTaskHold until terminal, never invents recoverable credential storage.

The UIKit adapter restores the previous native delegate on dismantle and forwards the four dismissal callbacks; the broader optional-adaptation question remains conditional and is not mislabelled a proven iPad regression.
